# My plan for this year

Well, I've been farming these 10.9 mu for thirty years, and my father farmed them before me. I do what I know works. Wheat in the fall, maize in the summer, same as everyone in the village. I can't read those papers the extension people bring around, but I know my fields.

## Wheat (my main crop through the winter)

I'll plant all 10.9 mu to wheat in early October, right after we clear the maize off. The ground has to be plowed and smoothed first — I pay the tractor man from the next village about 50 yuan per mu to run his rotary tiller over it. I don't own any big machinery. Too expensive for a small plot like mine.

For seed I use what the township shop sells. I used to save my own seed but now everyone buys the new kind — I don't know the name but it's what the shop has. About 30 jin per mu (15 kg), costs maybe 5-6 yuan per jin.

Fertilizer — before I plant, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu. The three-fifteen kind, 40 kg bags. That's what I've always done. Then when the wheat wakes up in March and starts growing again, I spread some urea on top — maybe 30 jin per mu (15 kg). If the wheat looks yellow or thin, I'll put a little more. If it looks good and thick I save my money. My neighbor Old Wang last year put on less and his wheat was fine, but I'm not brave enough to cut back. My family needs the grain.

Water — my well works but electricity costs money. I irrigate once before winter so the wheat doesn't freeze, once in spring at jointing, and one more time when the grain is filling if it hasn't rained. That's three times most years. If the rains are bad I might need a fourth time but I hate to spend that money.

For the weeds I spray herbicide once in spring, the shop sells one that works on the broadleaf weeds. If I see aphids I'll spray something for that too. Not always — some years I skip it.

Harvest is in early June. I hire the combine, 50 yuan a mu, takes half a day and we're done. Used to cut it all by hand when I was younger — thirty years ago the whole family would be in the field for a week. Nobody does that anymore.

I expect maybe 800 jin per mu (400 kg). Good year 900, bad year 700. That's what my land does.

## Maize (right after the wheat)

Same fields, same 10.9 mu. As soon as the combine leaves and the straw is chopped, I plant maize directly into the stubble. No plowing — no time. Between the wheat harvest and getting maize in the ground I have maybe five days. I rent the seeding machine from a fellow in the village, he charges maybe 30 yuan a mu including the seed-with-fertilizer planting.

Maize seed is expensive — hybrid seed, about 50 yuan a kg, and I use around 2 kg per mu. But you have to use the new seed every year, can't save it, the shop people say it won't grow right. My neighbors all say the same.

At planting, the machine drops some compound fertilizer with the seed. Then when the maize is about knee-high, at jointing, I broadcast urea. Maybe 40 jin per mu (20 kg). That's the big feeding for maize. The plants show it — they turn dark green and grow fast.

Water — depends on the rain. Normal summer I maybe irrigate once around jointing if it's been dry. If we get good rains I don't irrigate at all. Maize in summer usually gets enough rain here.

Spray herbicide once after planting for the weeds. Watch for borers, if I see them I spray.

Harvest late September. Hire the combine again.

Expect maybe 1000 jin per mu (500 kg) for maize. It grows well in summer.

## About our family and money

We're six people but two of my sons work in the city — they send money home sometimes but they're not in the fields. My wife and I do most of the work. My old mother still helps a little with small jobs. My daughter-in-law helps at busy times if she's not working. A farm this small, we manage ourselves. Only hire out the machinery work.

Money is always tight. Total inputs for the year maybe 9,000 yuan for everything — fertilizer is the biggest cost, then the machine fees, then seeds. That's why I watch every bag of fertilizer. Old Li across the way he puts on more than me but he has relatives who run a fertilizer shop. I pay full price.
